headline: A Thanksgiving storm brings heavy rain with possible flash flooding in New York City, gusts up to about 60 mph across the city and Long Island Thursday afternoon and evening under a High Wind Warning, and widespread moderate coastal flooding at both Thursday high tides.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry around New York City with high pressure to the north and light east-northeast winds around 10 mph. Low clouds move into the city and Long Island's south shore around 1 AM Thursday, and winds strengthen steadily overnight, reaching 20 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40 mph by the Thursday morning commute.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The Thanksgiving storm is still on track, with the worst rain and wind most likely Thursday afternoon and evening within a window of roughly 10 AM to the overnight hours. A High Wind Warning runs from 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island and nearby northeast New Jersey, with gusts up to about 60 mph, while a Wind Advisory covers inland northeast New Jersey (now including western Passaic County), the lower Hudson Valley and southern Connecticut from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday with 45 to 55 mph gusts; both could end a few hours early if models come into better agreement. Rain totals have been raised, with the heaviest rain Thursday evening, a possible rumble of thunder, and a slight chance of 1-inch-per-hour downpours near New York City, which is at a Slight Risk for flash flooding (Marginal Risk elsewhere, where minor poor-drainage flooding is more likely). Drier air cuts the rain off Thursday evening, winds turn southerly and ease overnight, leaving light rain or drizzle into Friday morning, then a few light showers Friday afternoon with southwest gusts of roughly 30 to 40 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday is mainly dry but breezy, with west winds gusting to roughly 25 to 30 mph. Sunday looks quiet with good conditions. Monday brings a chance of showers with southwest gusts of about 25 to 30 mph, turning northwest in the afternoon; the discussion gives no temperature details for these days.

coast: Gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds Thursday morning into Thursday night bring widespread moderate coastal flooding at both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with a chance of major flooding along the western Great South Bay and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. Tides are running high after the recent full moon, and Thursday morning's tide is naturally higher by at least a foot, but the peak surge arrives Thursday afternoon and evening, so both tides may reach similar levels, and heavy rain during the evening tide could worsen coastal street flooding. Coastal Flood Warnings run 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM Friday for most of the coastline (southeastern Connecticut is under an advisory through 3 PM Friday), and a Coastal Flood Watch covers Friday's daytime high tide, when southwest winds may bring another round of moderate flooding to the southern bays of Long Island and Queens, especially the eastern Great South Bay, with minor flooding elsewhere. On the ocean beaches 8 to 12 foot breakers bring widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwash, while western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Gale Warning (6 PM Wednesday to 6 AM Thursday) gives way to a Storm Warning on all waters from 6 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas near 20 feet late Thursday afternoon and evening and waves up to about 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and below that Sunday.
watch_for: Exact timing of Thursday's peak winds and rain; warning end times may be trimmed by a few hours
Downpours and possible flash flooding in New York City Thursday evening, especially during the evening high tide
Water levels at Thursday's morning and evening high tides, and Friday morning's on the south shore bays
confidence: Confidence is high in a damaging-wind and coastal-flood event Thursday, but models still differ on timing by a few hours, and the coastal flood forecast deliberately leans toward the higher end for a safety margin; little detail is given beyond the weekend.
